draft.body:
Dear Professor Cha,

FACT’s combination of robot-friendly building operation and human–space interaction looks especially relevant to an architectural question I am developing (https://fact.kaist.ac.kr/).

For Proxy Society, I propose comparing a library’s shared queue with a side handoff bay for the same AI/robot collection task. A revoked mandate would require an immediate return to staff; waiting, detours and staff work would be observed alongside plans and sections.

Could this become a doctoral project through Future Space Lab, and what would its architectural contribution need to be within Culture Technology? I would value a short conversation about the experiment and degree route.

Best regards,
Kris Haamer

draft.subject: Public architectural research route for the Korean Architects Union
draft.body:
Dear UIA Secretariat,

Your member page names the Korean Architects Union in North Korea (https://www.uia-architectes.org/en/member/north-korea-korean-architects-union-kau/).

I am developing Proxy Society, an architectural research project on how civic-building thresholds accommodate people and AI/robot services acting for absent people. For the Korea research map, I am looking for published architectural scholarship or an appropriate professional introduction route, without assuming a local contact or doctoral opportunity.

Could UIA advise whether KAU has a public channel for such research enquiries, or suggest accessible publications and a suitable institutional intermediary? A referral or clarification of the available route would be helpful.

Best regards,
Kris Haamer
Proxy Society
https://proxysociety.org/architecture
